title: The minimal exact towers: the Sierpinski gasket, the slit triangle, and the Fano tower
claim: Let G be a single-scale exact gadget of a three-bit knot (m copies, h hidden variables, factor c, legs on three distinct copies pairwise at distance s), and T_k its tower: k times, every copy is replaced by a copy of G aligned to its constraint, with fresh hidden variables. Theorem 1: T_k has m^k copies and 3 + h(m^k - 1)/(m - 1) variables; its corner relation is the knot, with c^((m^k - 1)/(m - 1)) extensions per allowed tuple, so the corner law of a uniform solution is the same at every level; distances between variables of T_(k-1) scale by s, so the corners are at distance s^k, and if every variable of G is within s of each leg and every copy of G holds a variable within s - 1 of each leg, the ball of radius s^j around a corner holds exactly 3 + h(m^j - 1)/(m - 1) variables (growth exponent log m / log s); T_k has a tree decomposition of width h + 2 and every sub-tower is cut off by its three corners. Theorem 2: with weight r on excluded tuples, each excluded leg tuple of an exact gadget with legs on distinct copies gets weight at least 3c r + O(r^2) against c + O(r) for allowed ones, so the hard law repels softening. Theorem 3: the parity triangle, (m, h, s, c) = (3, 3, 2, 2), the twisted not-all-equal punctured tetrahedron (4, 3, 2, 2) and the not-all-equal punctured Fano plane (7, 6, 3, 5) have growth exponents log2 3, 2 and log3 7 and softened maps r(r^2 + 3)/(3r^2 + 1), 4r/(1 + r)^2 and r(r^6 + 7r^3 + 21r + 35)/(r^6 + r^5 + 2r^4 + 9r^3 + 20r^2 + 26r + 5), each with multiplier m at r = 0 and r < r' < 1 on (0, 1), so every softened tower flows to the free law; at the hard law two corners share 0 bits (parity) or 5/3 - log2 3 bits (the other two) at every distance s^k.
failure_conditions: A tower level whose copy or variable count, corner distances, eccentricities or ball sizes differ from Theorem 1.
A level whose corner counts differ from c^((m^k - 1)/(m - 1)) on an allowed tuple or are nonzero on an excluded one.
A copy outside the bag of its parent node, a variable whose bags are not a subtree, or a node whose three corners do not cut off what it introduced.
A softened weight polynomial or factorization differing from Theorem 3, a multiplier other than m, or an excluded tuple with fewer than 3c one-violation extensions.
foundation_claim_scope: The three smallest single-scale exact gadgets of parity, twisted not-all-equal and not-all-equal (from EXACT-TOWERS-20261029-001A and HUB-SURVIVORS-20261029-001B) and the towers they generate by substitution with private hidden variables; Theorem 1 for every single-scale exact gadget, Theorem 2 for every exact gadget with legs on distinct copies. Checked to levels 6, 5 and 4 (exact counts to 4, 3 and 3). Counts are a branch-internal measure; growth exponents are graph volume growth, not manifold dimension.

validation.status: checked: the three gadgets (knot relations, uniform counts, legs on distinct copies at one distance, the two distance conditions); towers to levels 6, 5 and 4 with copies, variables, corner distances, eccentricities and ball sizes as stated; exact corner counts by variable elimination to levels 4, 3 and 3 (up to 5^57 per allowed tuple); hierarchy tree decompositions of width h + 2 and three-corner cuts at every node; softened weight polynomials, factorizations, sampled positivity and multipliers 3, 4, 7; controls fire (a drifting non-exact rebuild, the shared-midpoint grid not cut off, a mutated Fano gadget not exact); no human or external review
